purpose: Machine-checkable record of every source file this candidate repository was built from, the responsibility units inside those files, the single feature and the one owning package of each adopted behaviour, and the rights that apply. Audited by scripts/audit_inventory.py; human-readable lineage lives in PROVENANCE.md and upstream notices live in NOTICE.

craft.name: craft-skills

license.evidence: No LICENSE, COPYING, or NOTICE file exists at this revision, and no inventoried file carries a licence header. The only licence statement is the string "MIT" in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and .codex-plugin/plugin.json, and that repository's own README states MIT is declared in the plugin manifest with no LICENSE file present. Metadata without the copyright line and permission text is not a grantable MIT notice.

craft.rights: Read as behavioural and requirements evidence only. No code, prose, table, checklist, example, asset, or corpus string from this source is copied into or redistributed by this repository; every adopted behaviour was re-expressed from the requirement it encodes, grounded in public vendor documentation cited per package.

upstream.name: obsidian-skills

license.evidence: Repository-root LICENSE at this revision carries the full MIT text: the copyright line, the permission grant, the notice-retention condition, and the warranty disclaimer. .claude-plugin/plugin.json independently declares "license": "MIT" with author Steph Ango.

upstream.rights: MIT. Files marked mit-import are copied and modified derivatives; the copyright line and the complete permission notice are retained in the repository-root LICENSE and restated per file in NOTICE. Files marked mit-reference were read for convention only and contributed no copied text.

units.behavior: Requests to write, edit, or reformat note prose, links, embeds, callouts, properties, tags, and house style resolve to the Obsidian Flavored Markdown owner.
Requests to create, debug, or optimise a .base file or an embedded base block resolve to the Bases owner.
Requests to create or edit a .canvas JSON Canvas graph resolve to the Canvas owner.
Requests to author or repair Mermaid that must render inside Obsidian resolve to the Mermaid owner.
Requests to create or extend a note-grounded Excalidraw or Canvas visualisation by writing the file directly resolve to the visualisation owner.
Requests to read, create, search, move, mutate, or link-audit vault notes from a terminal resolve to the official CLI owner.
Requests to build or debug an Obsidian Web Clipper JSON template resolve to the Clipper owner.
Requests to diagnose a plugin, a template, a plugin API skew, or a plugin-driven script resolve to the diagnosis owner.
Requests to bootstrap, pair, operate, or recover the headless sync client resolve to the sync owner.
Reading sync state for a vault the desktop app already syncs is a read-only command-surface operation, kept separate from headless pairing and daemon lifecycle.

One description carried the trigger surface for all nine features at once. Here each package carries its own description and its own out-of-scope clause, so discovery never depends on a shared router entry.
units.notes: Splitting the description is a packaging decision shared by all nine features, not a behaviour any single feature owns.

units.behavior: Return the verified artefact or runtime state, the evidence, and every unavailable prerequisite; stop instead of inventing an operation. Each package states this for its own surface.
An exact vault root must be resolved from the environment or the task before filesystem readback; no vault name or path is ever hardcoded.
The source required discovering four external format and CLI packages by identity through the host skill loader and refusing to answer format questions locally.
units.reason: This repository ships nine independent packages that each own their format or command surface outright. There is no loader discovery, dispatcher, or mandatory neighbour, so the discovery requirement has no counterpart here; optional composition by explicit identity is the only remaining form.

units.behavior: Drawing files are produced by a standard-library Python generator, with no third-party dependency and no plugin runtime required to author a scene.
An active drawing plugin and its automation API are prerequisites only for rendered image export and live-edit work; plugin installation, enablement, and settings changes stay separate effects.
Headless sync work requires the headless client binary from its npm package, identified and version-gated before any pairing step.
A real page fetch or browser session is required whenever a clipper selector must be proven against the live page rather than assumed.
Mutable app, CLI, plugin API, and sync facts are grounded in official documentation, recorded with the observed version, and re-checked on release change before a package claims them.
No host path, vault name, account identifier, remote host, or credential appears in any shipped file; examples are synthetic and public.

units.source_anchor: composition paragraph after the route table
units.behavior: Two packages compose only when their responsibilities genuinely differ; composition is by explicit identity and stays optional.
Resolve the exact artefact, read before writing, preserve unrelated content, use the least destructive surface, read back the result, report evidence, and keep unresolved runtime facts unknown.
Format capability never grants write authority; the destination vault's own policy owns authorisation, placement, and house style.

A closing checklist separates target resolution, preservation, destructive scope, readback, and unverified runtime claims. Each package carries its own checklist and the repository keeps a cross-package matrix.
The source warned against loading every sub-recipe for every request.
units.reason: Selective sub-recipe loading is a property of a single thick package. Here the host loads one small package per task, so there is no shared body to over-load and no counterpart rule to carry.

units.behavior: Vault notes are never edited with shell redirection or stream editors; the host editing tool or the selected vault-aware surface performs the write and the file is read back afterwards.
The source forbade restating a native format or command catalogue locally and required reporting a capability gap instead.
units.reason: Inverted by design here: each package is the local owner of its format or command catalogue, so the rule against local catalogues does not carry over. What is kept is the narrower rule that a package reports a capability gap instead of inventing a surface it does not own.

units.behavior: A skill name that looks like an executable is not that executable; a similarly named third-party tool is never substituted for the official binary.
A tool is not declared unavailable on one failed probe; a second, different probe must confirm before a degraded path is reported.
Markdown, .base, .canvas, and Mermaid are separate parsers with separate invariants and are never treated as one syntax. Each package description names the artefacts it excludes.
A requested drawing is not silently replaced by a different visual form or a screenshot, the format rule decides between graph and freeform, and compressed drawing payloads are never hand-edited.
A clipper selector is never shipped on assumption; the page is inspected and every selector is verified before the template is delivered.
Plugin state files and bundled plugin code are not edited directly; the diagnosis pipeline uses the plugin's or runtime's supported mutation surface.
Bidirectional or continuous sync is never enabled before a one-shot pull-only run has been compared and accepted.
A reusable package never decides a personal vault's taxonomy, filing zone, or house style; that belongs to the vault's own policy owner.
The official app binary, not a similarly named third-party tool, is the default command surface, and the installed binary's own help output is the source of the command list.
The diagnosis pipeline uses only commands the installed binary actually documents; invented plugin and note subcommands are removed and an edit is composed from the real write surface.
Read-only sync state for an app-managed vault is handed to the command surface, while pairing, promotion, supervisor lifetime, and incident recovery stay with the headless sync owner.

Three field-derived guards: empty output with exit code zero is indeterminate and must be retried, no tool is declared unavailable after a single probe, and every command claim names the binary that produced it.
Vault resolution uses the supported registry lookup and an explicit target mapping instead of probing an obsolete default vault, and it never silently changes a configured default.
Eight separate Obsidian packages were consolidated into one thick package with selectively loaded sub-recipes, and that entry also claims a third-party lineage for the pre-consolidation material.
units.reason: This repository takes the opposite shape on purpose: nine independent packages, no router and no shared runtime. The entry is inventoried because it is the rights-relevant record: the claimed third-party lineage carries no licence evidence, which is one more reason no expression from this source is copied here. No claim is made about that third party's material.

units.behavior: Mutable runtime behaviour is answered from official documentation first, conflicts are disclosed, and an unresolved fact stays unknown rather than being guessed.
Official sources and safely observed versions are recorded with the change that used them, and affected evaluations are re-run when they move.
Evidence that a runtime form changed triggers a documentation re-check, affected evaluations, a recipe update, then a version bump and a changelog entry.

Bases guidance answers how to embed a named view and the rename hazard that selector creates, how to extract a base's rows, which layouts a given app version has, and which grouping limits are current engine constraints rather than historical artefacts.
A shared tool preflight distinguishes the official binary from a community binary of a similar name before any command runs, and the stop condition is stated once.

A package never links out of its own directory, because a distribution fetcher treats an escaping relative path as traversal and refuses to install it; cross-package references name the owning package and file in prose instead.
Trimming a description to fit a length cap must not remove a trigger phrase an asserted routing case depends on; removed triggers are a breaking change, not a cosmetic edit.
A link or embed written into a note is resolved and read back from the source note's own context, and a resolution failure is reported rather than inferred from the note's whole unresolved-link set.
Static base validity, materialised file state, and what the app actually renders are separate claims; a missing app or view is reported as unverified rather than assumed to render.
A canvas referenced or embedded from a note keeps its documented render limits, and exact file readback is reported separately from any rendering claim.
Command mechanics, argument grammar, and fallback behaviour belong to one owner instead of being restated in a coordinating layer.

Format and command ownership sits with the package that owns the artefact, and a coordinating layer keeps only authorisation, readback, and capability-gap reporting. Here that is expressed as optional composition by explicit identity between independent packages, with no mandatory discovery step.
A note-grounded visualisation route exists with admission checks, exact-target additive persistence, reload, linking, and rendering boundaries, and it leaves command grammar to the command owner.

Writing the drawing file directly with a deterministic generator is the default, because building through a live plugin API was slow and corrupted an existing drawing; an automated identifier, binding, and overlap check runs before any rendered check.
Note writes are authorised by the destination vault's policy and performed with the host editing tool or the selected vault-aware surface; no bundled mutation service is named as the write authority.
The source deferred all Markdown syntax to an external package and reported a capability gap when that package was absent.
units.reason: The Markdown feature owns its syntax outright in this repository, so there is no external owner to defer to and no absence to report. The capability-gap discipline survives only for surfaces a package genuinely does not own, which is recorded on the corresponding anti-pattern unit.

units.behavior: Before any note write the vault root, the vault-relative target, the named effect, and the authority for it must all be known; behaviour stays read-only until then, and existing task-bound authority is reused rather than re-requested.

units.source_anchor: Non-Markdown targets and destination readback section
units.behavior: A link to a non-Markdown file keeps its extension because a bare stem resolves to a different target, and the written link is resolved from the source note's context and read back before it is reported as working.
units.notes: The canvas feature re-derived the same requirement for .canvas artefacts in its own operations reference; that adoption is recorded in its package changelog and is a composition, not a second owner.

units.behavior: Note meaning, filing, template choice, and provenance belong to the vault's policy owner rather than to a format package, and the closing checks separate authorisation, preservation, and readback.
The source deferred embed syntax to one external package and canvas structure to another.
units.reason: Both surfaces are owned locally here, by the Markdown feature and the Canvas feature respectively, so there is no external deferral to carry over.

units.behavior: A canvas embedded in a note renders only the documented subset of its content, so the embed is written with that limit stated and the rendered result is never claimed from file state alone.
Authorisation for the target vault, app and renderer evidence for a base or an embedded base block, and the separation of static validity from what the app displays.

A command surface does not grant write authority: the exact vault, the authorised effect, and the mutation surface are resolved first, and the result is proven by materialised readback rather than by exit status.

A diagram family is only used when the target app's bundled renderer supports it; compatibility is never inferred from another tool or a live editor, and a rejected family falls back without dropping meaning.
A catalogue of copy-ready diagram families, each marked with the version gate it needs and the fallback to use when the gate fails, instead of reconstructing grammar from memory.
units.notes: The source file credits its examples to an unnamed third-party collection with no resolvable link or licence notice. No example text was carried forward and no rights claim is made over that collection.

units.behavior: The visual form is chosen by a stated rule: existing vault notes as nodes select the graph format, freeform illustration selects the drawing format, and an explicit user request wins over the default.

The drawing file is a documented text shape with a readable element index and one embedded scene payload, and element essentials such as identifiers, geometry, and bindings are set deliberately rather than by imitation.
The canvas file's node and edge structure, identifiers, and geometry are owned by the canvas format owner rather than restated inside a visualisation recipe.
Generate the file, validate it programmatically, then confirm it renders, and report which of those three claims was actually reached.
The plugin automation path is reserved for edits inside a drawing the user has open and for embeds that must pass through the plugin's file store; everything else writes the file directly.
Scene content is grounded in the notes it claims to represent, and an existing drawing is extended additively without rewriting unrelated elements or hand-editing compressed payloads.

The live-edit exception path: admit the plugin API only after checking it is present, persist additively to the exact open drawing, guard asynchronous completion instead of assuming it, then reload and check the rendered result.

A standard-library scene builder produces a drawing file deterministically and exposes a separate defect check for duplicate identifiers, broken bindings, and overlapping elements, so validation is mechanical rather than visual.
units.notes: The shipped generator is independently authored: 54439 bytes against the source file's 12194, a different module contract (deterministic identifiers, Unicode-aware text measurement, finite-geometry checks) and a different digest. No line of the source script is reused.

units.behavior: The end-to-end clipper recipe: decide when a template is the right answer, verify selectors against the real page, align frontmatter with the vault's existing note type, and name the rationalisations and red flags that produce a one-off template.
The importable template document: its root fields, note-content body, property list with declared types, and the validation a template must pass before import.
The variable families a template can read - preset page values, prompt values, selector values, meta values, and structured page data - and the fallback behaviour when one is empty.
Filters transform a variable in a chain, and the pitfalls that actually break output - notably converting already-converted content twice - are stated with the source type each filter expects.
Conditionals, loops, assignment, and fallbacks inside the template body and property values, used to keep optional sections out of a note when the data is absent.
Fetch a representative page, inspect what the page actually exposes, prefer structured page data over brittle selectors, and prove every variable resolves before the template is delivered.
A clipped note reuses the property definitions the vault's existing base for that content type already declares, so the clip lands with the same frontmatter as every other note of its type.
A neutral general-purpose clipping template demonstrating the document shape a user can import and adapt.
units.notes: The shipped asset is independently authored from the official Web Clipper documentation, with schema facts checked against the MIT-licensed obsidianmd/obsidian-clipper source at 6d56d618b00bd970aa738d6a7a61edee27783e81. Nothing is copied from the source asset and nothing from the clipper application is vendored.

units.behavior: A second neutral template showing structured page data driving typed properties and a conditional body, so the two assets together cover both the simple and the data-driven shape.
units.notes: Independently authored; see the note on the general template asset.

units.behavior: A bounded diagnosis loop: inspect what is installed, classify the symptom, consult a registry of known plugin behaviour, fetch fresh documentation on a miss, patch through a supported surface, verify against real error output, and record the finding for the next run.

Each pipeline step states its command forms, its expected output shape, its classification decision tree, its pass and escalation criteria, and the handoff to the next step, so a failed step stops the pipeline instead of degrading it.

A seed registry keyed by plugin identifier, with append-only known-pattern, anti-pattern, and regression lists, an observed-version field, and an explicit rule that host-specific or vault-specific paths never enter it.

Every sync change is staged, evidenced, and reversible: resolve both ends of the pairing exactly, start in pull-only, run once, compare the local difference before believing it, and promote to continuous or bidirectional mode only on request.
The headless client's install, version, setup, configuration, and run commands, the shape of its configuration file, and what its common error messages actually mean.

A process supervisor owns process lifetime and the sync client owns sync configuration; the registered supervisor is inspected and preserved rather than replaced, and a point-in-time backup stays a separate system from sync.

Incident handling order: contain first, preserve evidence second, restore only when needed and authorised, and re-admit continuous sync only after a clean staged run. A diagnosis never authorises reset, unlink, account changes, or supervisor replacement.
Creating a note through the command surface must use the official binary, resolve the vault and note path, and read the exact result back afterwards.
The official app binary and the similarly named third-party binary must be named as two distinct tools with non-interchangeable command surfaces.

Asked where a personal note belongs, a package must decline and name the policy owner instead of inventing a taxonomy. Every one of the nine packages must hold this line, so it is a shared boundary rather than one feature's behaviour.
Empty output with exit code zero is not a count of zero: it is retried, then reported as indeterminate with the retry outcome and the binary that produced it.
A single failed lookup does not make a tool unavailable, and it never justifies a filesystem fallback; a second different probe must run before any degraded path is reported.
A new drawing is written as a file by a generator and checked for identifier, binding, and overlap defects before anything is opened; the live plugin path is not used for new work.
A map of existing vault notes selects the graph format, and the graph schema itself is left to the canvas owner rather than reinvented in the visualisation package.
A Korean-language request to tidy up an Obsidian note must reach the Markdown owner, so its description carries non-English note-cleanup phrasing.
A request to create a base must reach the Bases owner.
A request to repair a canvas graph file must reach the Canvas owner.
A request to make a diagram render inside Obsidian must reach the Mermaid owner, whose acceptance surface is the app's bundled renderer.
A request to move a note from the command line must reach the CLI owner, including when the user names the command by the third-party spelling.
A request to debug a misbehaving plugin must reach the diagnosis owner.
A request to repair a Web Clipper template must reach the Clipper owner.
A sync status request must reach the sync owner, which also decides when the answer is a read-only state query handed to the command surface.
A request to audit unresolved links in a vault must reach the CLI owner, whose link-audit commands answer it.
A Korean-language backlinks check must also reach the CLI owner, so its description is not English-only.
Extracting a web article is not clipper work: the Clipper owner builds templates and must exclude page extraction in its own description.
A diagram for a website does not inherit the app's bundled-renderer baseline, so the Mermaid owner declares out-of-app rendering out of scope.
Generic file synchronisation, version-control conflicts, and backup systems are a different system from vault sync and are excluded by the sync owner.
Installing the desktop application is a host effect, not a command-surface operation; the CLI owner treats a missing app or binary as a reported capability gap instead.

Five prompts that no Obsidian package may claim: personal vault taxonomy, browser dashboards, authoring a repository contract file, querying a web API, and writing a pull-request description. No single feature owns these exclusions; all nine must hold them.

A root contract states what each package owns, that required references and assets live inside the owning package, that upstream notices and exact revisions are recorded, that examples stay synthetic and public, that missing runtime evidence is never turned into success, and that local candidate work does not authorise publication or retirement of another owner.
A root readme documents per-runtime installation, the package list, and how a host discovers the packages, so a reader can install without reading the installer script.

The source's own licence section states that MIT is declared in its plugin manifest and that no LICENSE file exists in the repository. This is the primary evidence for treating that source as unlicensed for copying purposes, and this repository answers it by shipping a real root LICENSE plus a NOTICE.
One installer script copies the package set into several agent-runtime skill directories, resolves per-runtime scopes and paths, prints a plan before acting, and refuses to clobber unrelated content.

A plugin manifest carries name, description, version, author, homepage, repository, and licence fields. It is also the source's only machine-readable licence statement, which is why its contents are recorded here as rights evidence.
A marketplace manifest names the catalogue, its owner, and one plugin entry pointing at the repository root.
A second runtime's manifest adds a skills directory pointer and a presentation block with display name, category, capabilities, and example prompts.
A third runtime's marketplace entry declares a local source path and an installation and authentication policy.

A single registry table records, per package, the origin, the upstream repository and revision, and the relationship - derived, adapted, vendored, or original - with dated per-change detail kept in each package changelog and never in the recipe body. This repository follows the same split between a root provenance record and per-package changelogs.

The Obsidian Flavored Markdown recipe: note workflow, wikilinks and block identifiers, embeds, callouts, frontmatter properties, tags, comments, inline formatting, mathematics, footnotes, a complete worked note, and the official documentation links.
units.notes: Imported and then extended; the shipped file adds target resolution, preservation, non-Markdown link targets, destination readback, anti-patterns, and a verification checklist. MIT notice retained in the root LICENSE and restated in NOTICE.

units.behavior: A diagram lives in a fenced mermaid block inside the note, and diagram nodes link to notes through the documented internal-link class.
units.notes: The Mermaid feature owns fence grammar, nesting, and the internal-link behaviour. The imported section also survives inside the Markdown derivative, where it stays covered by the same MIT notice; the Mermaid package re-derived its rules from public Mermaid and Obsidian documentation.

units.behavior: Callout syntax, foldable and nested callouts, the supported type table with aliases and colours, and the custom-style snippet.
units.notes: Imported unchanged, then extended with structure rules, an intent-to-type table, unrecognised-type behaviour, a failure table, and a checklist.

units.behavior: Embed forms for notes, headings and blocks, images with sizing, external images, audio, PDF, base, and list embeds, plus the search-result block.
units.notes: Imported unchanged, then extended with subpath exactness, self-embed cycles, pipe semantics, a canvas-embed section, media caveats, a failure table, and a checklist.

units.behavior: The frontmatter example, the property type table, the default property list, and the tag character rules.
units.notes: Imported unchanged, then extended with placement rules, per-type value shapes, link quoting and readback, a safe-edit procedure, a failure table, and a checklist.

units.behavior: The Bases recipe: file schema, global and per-view filters with their operators, the three property kinds and the file-property reference, formula syntax and duration arithmetic, view types, summary formulas, embedding, quoting rules, and troubleshooting.
units.notes: MIT import; the shipped package records its exact modifications in its own changelog.

units.behavior: The function reference for base formulas, grouped by receiver type with signatures and return types.

The canvas recipe: file structure, the four node kinds with their attributes, edges and their anchors, the colour presets, identifier generation, geometry and layout guidance, and a validation checklist.
units.notes: MIT import with the package renamed and a local scope, identifier-collision, operations, and attribution addition; the format content is preserved.

units.behavior: Four complete canvas documents - text with connections, a project board with groups, a research canvas with file and link nodes, and a flowchart - usable as copy-ready starting points.
units.notes: The four example documents are byte-identical to this pinned source; the package changelog records the digest comparison and the added title, introduction, and attribution.

units.behavior: The official command-line recipe: argument syntax, file and vault targeting, common note and property patterns, and the plugin and theme development cycle with its reload, evaluate, error, screenshot, and inspect commands.
units.notes: MIT import, then substantially extended with binary identity, authorisation, mutation contract, failure branches, and version-skew handling verified against an installed build.

units.behavior: The MIT licence text governing every imported upstream file: copyright line, permission grant, notice-retention condition, and warranty disclaimer.
units.notes: Retained twice: the copyright line appears in the repository-root LICENSE alongside this repository's own line, and NOTICE restates it with the exact list of imported files it covers.

units.behavior: Installation documented per runtime - marketplace command, package-manager command, and manual copy into each runtime's skills directory - with the specification the packages follow.
units.notes: Read for convention only. No sentence is copied; this repository documents its own installer and its own package set.

units.behavior: A plugin manifest declaring name, version, description, author, repository, licence, and keywords. It corroborates the MIT declaration for the imported files.
A marketplace manifest naming the catalogue, its owner, and a single plugin entry rooted at the repository.

excluded.reason: Sibling craft skills for unrelated domains. None of the nine Obsidian features derives behaviour from them, and no file, rule, or example was read into this repository.
Eval corpora belonging to the excluded sibling skills. Only the Obsidian corpus is in scope, and it is inventoried unit by unit.
Internal execution plans, governance reports, and research notes. Internal planning material is deliberately not reproduced, summarised, or referenced in this repository's public artefacts.

CI workflows, git hooks, agent host configuration, the test-tree package marker, and repository automation. This repository ships its own installer, tests, and audit tooling and adopts no gate or hook from the source.
Upstream packages for web-page extraction and a third-party layout plugin. Neither is one of the nine features, neither was imported, and no MIT rights are exercised over them here.
